sentences.text: Both insurer as well as claimants are in appeal questioning the liability as well as praying for enhancement of compensation respectively.

Both appeals arise from MVC No.734/2014 dated 29.02.2016 on the file of Addl.Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Ranebennur (for short,
'Tribunal').

sentences.text:
The claimant-Balachandra filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 claiming compensation for the accidental injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 20.05.2014 involving lorry bearing registration No.KA-14/A-8318 and bus bearing registration No.KA-14/B-155.
It is submitted that the claimant suffered amputation above knee of both lower legs and he was inpatient for more than 52 days for treatment.

It NC:
2024:KHC-D:3618-DB is submitted that the claimant was earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month in terms of Ex.P14.
4.

On issuance of notice, insurer filed its objection statement denying the entire petition averments,
but admitted the policy.
It contended that as on the date of accident, injured person had no valid permit and driver of the bus had no valid and effective driving licence.
Accident is the result of rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the lorry.
On the above contentions, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
5. Petitioner examined himself as PW1.
He examined four witnesses as PWs.10 to 13 and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P15, P59 to P71 and Exs.P78 to P85.

The Tribunal on the material on record awarded total compensation of Rs.18,29,600/- on the following heads along with interest @
6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

1. For pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
2.

Medical expenses Rs.4,08,000/-
3. Conveyance, diet, extra Rs.80,000/-
nourishment
charges
food and NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB attendant charges

4. Future attendant charges Rs.1,00,000/-
5. Loss of income during laid up Rs.42,000/-
period 6.

Loss of future earning Rs.9,99,600/-
 capacity on account of  permanent physical disability 7. Loss of amenities and Rs.1,00,000/-
 enjoyment of life

Total Rs.18,29,600/-

sentences.text: 6. The Tribunal while awarding above compensation assessed the income of the injured appellant at Rs.7,000/- per month and assessed the whole body disability at 70%.

7. Heard Sri S.V.Yaji, learned counsel for the Insurance Company, Sri Girish S.Hulmani, learned counsel for the claimants and perused the appeal papers along with certified copies of the original records made available by learned counsel for claimants.

8. Learned counsel for the insurer would submit that the judgment and award of the Tribunal is unsustainable and Tribunal committed grave error in saddling entire liability on the insurer, since bus had no permit.
Moreover, he submits NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB that driver of the insured bus had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Learned counsel would submit that the Tribunal is not right or justified in saddling the liability on the insurer of the bus.

Further,
learned counsel would submit that the Tribunal rightly assessed the income of the injured appellant at Rs.7,000/- per month.
Further he submits that it is a head on collusion and Tribunal ought to have assessed contributory negligence, since accident had occurred in the middle of the road.

Further, learned counsel would submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on other heads are proper and correct and prays for dismissal of the appeal filed by the claimant and to allow the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimant would submit that the income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- per month is on the lower side and the Tribunal ought to have taken note of Ex.P14 and assessed income at Rs.10,000/- including bhatta.

PW12 is the employer who deposed before the Tribunal in respect of Ex.P14 and thus he NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB submits that Ex.P14-salary certificate is proved which the Tribunal ought to have taken note and assessed income of the injured at Rs.10,000/- per month.

Further, learned counsel would submit that though the Tribunal has come to a conclusion that functional disability of the claimant is 100%, assessed the whole body disability at 70% and awarded compensation, which is highly erroneous.
Learned counsel would submit that when the functional disability is 100%, the compensation shall be computed taking note of 100% functional disability.
Thus, he prays for re-assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month and to re- assess the compensation taking 100% functional disability.
Further, learned counsel would submit that the compensation awarded on other heads are also on the lower side, since the claimant was inpatient for 52 days.
It is submitted that claimant was aged 26 years and the multiplier adopted at '17' is proper.

Learned counsel would submit that in view of amputation of both legs above knee, marriage prospects of the claimant is affected and he would pray for compensation NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB on the said head also.
Thus, he prays for allowing the appeal of the claimant.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers including the Tribunal records i.e. certified copies of the records made available by learned counsel for the claimant during the course of hearing, the following points would arise for our consideration.
i.
Whether the Tribunal is justified in assessing the income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/- per month?

5 ii.

sentences.text: Whether the Tribunal is justified in assessing permanent disability of claimant at 70% for computation of compensation?
iii. Whether the claimant would be entitled for enhanced compensation?

11. Our answer to the above Point Nos.(i) and (ii) are 'in the negative and Point No.(iii) 'in the affirmative' for the following reasons.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB 12.

The accident that occurred on 20.05.2014 involving lorry bearing registration No.KA-14/A-8318 and bus bearing registration No.KA-14/B-155 and resultant injury sustained by the claimant is not in dispute in this appeal.
The insurer is in appeal questioning the entire liability, whereas the claimant is in appeal praying for enhancement of compensation.
13. Learned counsel for the insurer submitted that the insured bus for which the Insurance Company had insured had no permit as on the date of accident.
The insurer has failed to prove the said contention and on the other hand material on record would indicate that the bus in question had the permit.
It is to be noted that in terms of Ex.R4, one Sri B.V.Mohanraj in favour of whom bus was leased by Sri B.V.Narahari, permit is granted and the permit was valid on the date of accident.
Taking note of Ex.R4, we are not inclined to accept the contention of the insurer that the bus had no permit.
Further, learned counsel for the insurer contended that the accident had taken place in the middle of the road and it is head on collusion.
Therefore, the Tribunal - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB ought to have considered contributory negligence.
The said contention also cannot be accepted and the Tribunal is justified in saddling the entire liability on the insurance company.
Charge sheet is filed against the driver of the bus.
Moreover, either the driver of the bus or driver of the lorry is examined to establish the said contention.
Merely contending that the accident has occurred in the middle of the road, the Tribunal could not come to the conclusion that both the drivers contributed their negligence to the accident.
Hence, the said contention is also rejected.

14. Further, learned counsel for the insurer contended that Ex.P14-salary certificate states that the deceased was working as cleaner with the lorry bearing registration No.KA-14/A-8318 and further it indicates that injured was receiving salary of Rs.10,000/- including the bhatta.
Learned counsel for the insurer would submit that bhatta is to be deducted, only actual wages to be taken for calculation of compensation.

The said contention is liable to be rejected on the reason that the claim petition is filed u/sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act and compensation is to - 12 - The Divisionial Manager vs Balachandra on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29419586/
6 NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB be determined based on the income which the claimant was receiving or earning as on the date of accident.
The salary certificate would indicate that the claimant was receiving total salary of Rs.10,000/- per month.

Therefore, based on Ex.P14, the Tribunal ought to have assessed income of the claimant at Rs.10,000/- per month and Tribunal committed grave error in assessing the income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/- per month.

15 . Further, the Tribunal having come to the conclusion that the claimant suffers from 100%
functional disability ought to have assessed the compensation taking note of 100% permanent functional disability.
Admittedly, the claimant was working as cleaner in lorry.
As both legs of the appellant-claimant is amputed above knee, claimant would not be in a position to carry out the same work which he was carrying out prior to the incident i.e. work of cleaning.
Functional disability is to be assessed in relation to the work that was carried on by the injured prior to the accident.
When a person suffers 100% functional disability, naturally it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB compensation taking 100% functional disability.
Therefore, we assess the permanent disability of the claimant at 100%.
The multiplier adopted at '17' taking into age of the injured is proper and correct.

16. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Jagdish V/s Mohan and others1 at paragraph-11, it is held as follows:
"11.

In Govind Yadav v New India Insurance Company Limited, this Court adverted to the earlier decisions in R D Hattangadi v Pest Control (India) (Pvt) Ltd., Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences v Prasanth S Dhananka, Reshma Kumari v Madam Mohan, Arvind Kumar Mishra v New India Assurance Company Limited, and Raj Kumar v Ajay Kumar and held thus:
"18.

sentences.text: In our view, the principles laid down in Arvind Kumar Mishra v. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar must be followed by all the Tribunals and the High Courts in determining the quantum of compensation payable to the victims of accident, who are disabled either permanently or temporarily.

entities.text: Arvind Kumar Mishra v. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the victim of the accident suffers permanent disability, then efforts should always be made to award adequate compensation not only for the physical injury and treatment, but also for the loss of earning and his inability to lead a normal life and enjoy amenities, which he would have enjoyed but for the disability caused due to the accident."

These principles were reiterated in a judgment of this Court in The Divisionial Manager vs Balachandra on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29419586/
7 Subulaxmi v MD Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation12 delivered by one of us, Justice Dipak Misra (as the learned Chief Justice then was)."

sentences.text: In the instant case also, the appellant-claimant has lost both legs above knee and it would completely deprive of the ability to work as cleaner and his ability to earn.
Therefore, taking note of the age of the claimant-injured at 26 years, we deem it appropriate to award 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects.
Thus, the claimant would be entitled for following modified compensation on the head of loss of future income.

Rs.10,000(Income) + 40%(future prospects) x 12 (months) x 17 (multiplier) x 100% disability =
Rs.28,56,000/-.
17.

The compensation granted on the head of pain and suffering and loss of amenities enjoyment of life at Rs.1,00,000/- each is on the lower side when compared to amputation suffered and treatment taken as inpatient for 52 - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB days.

Therefore, in addition to what is granted, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
each is awarded on the said heads.
Taking re-assessed income of the claimant at Rs.10,000/- per month, loss of income during laid up period would be Rs.60,000/- as against Rs.42,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
18. The Tribunal committed an error in not awarding the compensation on the head of loss of marriage prospects and for artificial limbs.
Taking note of the injury/disability suffered by the claimant, we are of the view that the claimant has lost his marriage prospects.
When the claimant has lost his marriage prospects, any amount of compensation would not compensate.
However, we are of the view that the claimant-appellant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- on the head loss of marriage prospects and Rs.1,50,000/- each for artificial limbs to both legs.

Thus, the claimant would be entitled to modified compensation as under:
1. For pain and suffering Rs.2,00,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs.4,08,000/-
- 16 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB 3. Conveyance, diet, extra Rs.80,000/-
nourishment charges food and attendant charges 4.

Future attendant charges Rs.1,00,000/-

8

5. Loss of income during laid up Rs.60,000/-
period 6. Loss of future earning Rs.28,56,000/-
 capacity on account of  permanent physical disability 7. Loss of amenities and Rs.2,00,000/-
 enjoyment of life 8.

Towards marriage prospects Rs.3,00,000/-
9.

Future medical expenses (for Rs.3,00,000/-
 artificial limbs)
Thus, the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.45,04,000/- as against Rs.18,29,600/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, we pass the following order:
ORDER a.
MFA No.101686/2016 filed by the insurer is dismissed.
b. MFA No.102102/2016 filed by the claimant is allowed in part.

c. The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimant would be entitled to total - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3618-DB compensation of Rs.45,04,000/- as against Rs.18,29,600/- awarded by the Tribunal.
d. The enhanced compensation amount of shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till date of payment.

e. Respondent-Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount along with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
f. Deposit and disbursement of the enhanced compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
g. Registry to transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.
h. Draw modified award accordingly.
